title: Reset Git repository to last commit
summary: Discard all uncommitted changes and remove untracked files, restoring the project to the state of the last commit.

steps.explain: This command discards all changes in tracked files and removes untracked files. Be careful, as this action cannot be easily undone.

alternatives.explain: Short form for forcing the removal of untracked files.

warnings: This will permanently delete all uncommitted changes and untracked files.
Make sure you have backed up any important work before running this command.

rollback.explain: If you have not committed the changes you want to keep, there is no simple command to undo this. You may need to use `git reflog` if you had previously committed, but for uncommitted changes, recovery is often impossible.
